# LLM fundamentals

English · [Русский](../ru/themes/llm-fundamentals.md) · ← [AI Interview Atlas](../../README.md)

How transformers and LLMs work: attention, tokens, context, sampling, scaling. Engineers derive and implement; leaders need the intuition behind cost, quality and limits.

## Both tracks

- **Under a fixed training compute budget, how do Chinchilla-style scaling results change the balance between model size and training tokens?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †
  - Tests: Whether empirical training trade-offs are kept separate from deployment economics.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - State the fixed-compute setting and the empirical nature of the fit.
    - Balance parameter count with sufficient training tokens.
    - Separate training-optimal allocation from inference cost and data quality constraints.
  - Read: [Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15556) (Hoffmann et al., arXiv)
- **What objectives and data distinguish pretraining, instruction tuning and preference optimisation?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Meta](../companies/meta.md) †
  - Tests: Whether the candidate can identify what each stage can and cannot change.

## AI Engineering

- **Derive scaled dot-product attention and explain how its scale affects softmax gradients.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether tensor shapes and numerical behaviour support the explanation.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Track Q, K and V shapes through score computation and weighted summation.
    - Scale by the square root of key width; discuss saturation of softmax.
    - Apply the causal mask before softmax and check numerical stability.
  - Read: [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762) (Vaswani et al., arXiv)
- **Derive the memory required by a decoder's KV cache as batch size and context length grow.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Amazon](../companies/amazon.md) †, [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) †
  - Tests: Whether cache size is calculated from the actual architecture.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - For equal sequence lengths, use 2 × batch × layers × tokens × KV heads × head width × bytes.
    - Explain why queries are not retained for future decode steps.
    - Account separately for weights, activations, padding and allocation overhead.
  - Read: [Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06180) (Kwon et al., arXiv) · [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245) (Ainslie et al., arXiv)
- **Compare multi-head, multi-query and grouped-query attention in quality and serving memory.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Meta](../companies/meta.md) †
  - Tests: Whether shared keys and values are distinguished from query heads.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - MHA uses separate KV heads; MQA shares one; GQA shares within groups.
    - Relate KV-head count to cache size and memory reads.
    - Discuss quality evaluation and the need to train or adapt the checkpoint.
  - Read: [GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245) (Ainslie et al., arXiv)
- **Explain how latent attention compresses the KV representation and what must be reconstructed at inference.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether architectural compression is distinguished from lower numeric precision.
- **Why can an exact attention kernel run faster without changing the quadratic attention computation?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether memory traffic is separated from arithmetic complexity.
- **Explain BPE training and why numbers, source code and different writing systems can tokenize unevenly.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether tokenisation choices are connected to context use and representation.
- **Compare additive positional embeddings, rotary embeddings and attention biases for representing token order.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether different mechanisms for encoding position are understood.
- **Explain rotary position encoding and the trade-offs of interpolation when extending context beyond training lengths.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Meta](../companies/meta.md) †
  - Tests: Whether a longer accepted input is distinguished from reliable long-context reasoning.
- **How does sparse expert routing increase parameter capacity, and what costs remain despite activating only some experts?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether active computation, total memory and communication are separated.
- **Compare greedy decoding, beam search and temperature, top-k and nucleus sampling; give a failure mode for each.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) †, [Perplexity](../companies/perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether probability manipulation is connected to output diversity and quality.
- **How would you test and reduce a model's tendency to miss relevant evidence in the middle of a long context?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether context utilisation is measured rather than inferred from context capacity.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Move the same relevant evidence through controlled context positions.
    - Measure accuracy across lengths, distractors and model variants.
    - Compare retrieval, ordering and context reduction without assuming a universal cure.
  - Read: [Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172) (Liu et al., arXiv)
- **Compare pre-normalisation and post-normalisation transformer blocks, then explain what RMSNorm changes.**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether normalisation is linked to optimisation stability and its actual formula.
- **Explain the two branches of SwiGLU and the parameter and compute trade-offs against a conventional feed-forward block.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Meta](../companies/meta.md) †
  - Tests: Whether gated activations are explained beyond their name.
- **Trace the tensor shapes through one decoder-only transformer layer and through the final vocabulary projection.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †
  - Tests: Whether attention, residual paths and vocabulary logits form a coherent computation.
- **Relate cross-entropy, KL divergence and perplexity for next-token prediction; state the assumptions behind each comparison.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) †
  - Tests: Whether probabilistic definitions are used consistently.
- **Explain how self-attention cost grows with context length and compare ways to reduce that cost.**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) †
  - Tests: Whether efficiency changes are distinguished from changes to model behaviour.
